html:
A high-speed railway down the west coast of Taiwan, about 350 km from Taipei to Kaohsiung, opened in 2007. The fastest trains make the trip in about an hour and a half, against four hours or more on the old line.

The trains are a version of Japan's Shinkansen, the first time the bullet train was exported, while European firms supplied parts of the system. It was built by a private company under a contract to run it and later hand it back. Heavy debts led the government to step in and restructure the company in 2015.

The line links most of Taiwan's big cities, where the large majority of its people live, and has turned the west coast into something close to one long commuter belt. It came a few years before China's Beijing to Shanghai high-speed rail and the boom in fast trains across East Asia.
